public_rationale: The chess study supplies meaningful counterevidence to the claim that sequence models never learn functional representations. It does not settle the proposed explanation of general-purpose LLM failures. Neither failures alone nor a successful specialist model establishes the broad causal relationship Marcus asserts.
limitations: The strongest intervention evidence concerns a specialist chess model.
The distinction between a bounded functional representation and a 'proper' world model affects the assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs never induce proper world models, which causes them to be unable to play chess reliably and to make frequent stupid errors.

statement.excerpt: Critically, as I argued at the end of June (and going back to 2019) LLMs never induce proper world models, which is why, for example, they still can’t even play chess reliably,1 and continue to make stupid, head-scratching errors with startling regularity.
statement.document_title: LLMs are not like you and me—and never will be.

from_speaker: LLMs never induce proper world models
our_interpretation: Assess the explanation of existing capabilities at the post date, rather than treating 'never' as a separate forecast.
A functional world model represents relevant states and relationships and uses them to guide predictions or actions.
The causal assertion requires evidence connecting deficiencies in those representations to the specified errors. Observing errors alone is insufficient.
The period is the accumulated capability record through 2025-08-12. No lower bound is supplied because the assertion concerns what LLMs have ever learned.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled studies show that the relevant LLMs lack functional world representations and that this deficiency causes their chess failures and recurring errors, with plausible alternative explanations addressed.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Studies establish functional world representations in systems within the claim's scope and directly undermine the asserted explanation of their failures, or isolate a different explanation incompatible with the claimed causal mechanism.

evidence.explanation: The study reports learned chess-state representations that respond to interventions, challenging a blanket absence premise. Its specialist next-character model does not establish the cause of errors across general-purpose LLMs; the event date records the demonstrated capability as publicly documented.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Controlled experiments on the relevant pre-post LLMs that measure their representations and selectively alter them to test whether those changes explain chess failures and other specified errors.
